decisions.summary: Fresh block of 500 after each engine landing (background), 1,000 at T01 and close; SC-001's N = 500; the landing's own FR-009 fresh block stays the cohort gate's 48.
decisions.why: SC-001 leaves N to the plan at least 500, and 500 meets that. The FR-009 block being 48 is settled by the spec: FR-009's parenthetical names feature 415 D5's fresh block, which is FRESH=48, and only moves it before the push. Nothing in the request names a size. This should not be argued again.

decisions.summary: make fresh-tally reads dev/cohort-log and prints the pooled fresh rate by form and cause.
decisions.why: This is a measuring instrument for FR-001 and SC-001. It changes no behavior.

decisions.summary: The inventory's discovery method, with each entry sorted into pattern 1 (asked before placing, kept), 2 (placed then repaired) or 3 (asked only of the finished map), plus its share of R1's failures.
decisions.why: FR-002 requires each entry to state which of the rule's FOUR points it breaks. Those points are: asked of a candidate before placing; nothing placed and then repaired; a finished-map check only as a backstop (by the GM's amendment, in the cohort and tests only); and where no candidate is admitted, more room. The three patterns have no slot for point 4. A placer that drops, relaxes or refuses where the remedy is room (last_resort.py dropping ordinary lanes or raising WebRefused, SiteRefused, OverlapRefused as a backstop at record time) is not labeled as a point-4 breach. A rule coded twice is found ('every pair of functions judging one rule') but fits none of the patterns, and neither does a finished-map check run mid-map. XVI says the inventory decides the engine tasks, so an entry with no label is work with no task. That defeats FR-007, FR-006 and SC-003, and the GM's 'where else is this part of our algorithm?'. Nothing makes it necessary and nothing in the GM's words implies it. Fix: the patterns can stay as a grouping, but each entry must record which of the four points it breaks (or that it is coded twice). The discovery list must also name the sites where a placer that finds no admitted candidate drops, relaxes or refuses instead of being given room.

decisions.summary: make task-start refuses a task of a feature marked ON HOLD until feature NNN closes; HOLD_OK="<reason>" is a recorded escape.
decisions.why: The guard enforces FR-010, which is in scope. The escape is a carve-out of FR-010, which is absolute for claims tasks that change the engine. One use of the escape is implied by FR-010's own words 'that changes the engine': starting a NON-engine task of a held feature, which the guard over-blocks because it refuses every task. But D4 does not scope the escape, so any reason unlocks any task, including the engine tasks the GM put on hold ('put our claims work on hold ... before we start making adjustments'). Fix, one clause: HOLD_OK admits only a task that does not change the engine; using it on an engine task of a held feature breaks FR-010 and is not an escape.

decisions.summary: Engine tasks ordered by share of R1's failures (lane web, seating room, row/brook/grove rules, the rest), each designed in its Approach first.
decisions.why: The spec leaves the order open. The order changes nothing about what gets done, because every inventory group still gets a task.

decisions.summary: FR-003's principle text drafted at T03 and sent to the GM; the constitution amended only with the GM's words.
decisions.why: This is FR-003 as written ('in text the GM approves').

decisions.summary: A rule that cannot be asked before placing is a research question and goes to the record first.
decisions.why: As written, this does not exempt the rule from the request's 'anywhere'. It sends the case to research instead of keeping the rule audit-only. If such a rule then STAYS a finished-map-only check or a repair, that is an exception and needs its own MODE 1 ruling against the request.

decisions.summary: Baseline is T01's 1,000-seed block plus the fixed 48; before SC-001 a rebuild may re-deal maps provided the fresh rate does not rise, each newly failing seed diagnosed.
decisions.why: FR-009 makes the fresh-seed refusal start only once SC-001 is met, and FR-008 keeps the fixed, pinned and pool seeds passing at every landing, which the plan keeps. The 'rate must not rise' condition is an extra constraint the plan adds, not a relaxation.

decisions.summary: Per-task verification (reference map, make land, fresh 500); overlap through built-once indexes; deleted code deletes its tests; found defects become tasks here.
decisions.why: These are the project's standing practices, applied to the spec's FRs. They narrow nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: T01 measure, T02 hold guard, T03 inventory + principle draft, T04+ engine work by D5, T10 FR-009, T11 FR-011/SC-006, T12 close: 1,000 fresh, T106's seat turn re-applied (User Story 2), SC-004 delta, report.
decisions.why: The guards come after the engine work, as FR-009 and FR-011 require ('once SC-001 is met', 'after SC-001'). T12 re-applies feature 405's T106 seat turn before 417 closes. FR-010 holds 405's engine tasks until then, and the request puts 405's resumption after 417. The block cites the spec's User Story 2, which this bundle does not contain, so I could not check from here whether the spec settles it. I pass it on that citation: as a 417 robustness test it serves 'algorithms are brittle'. If User Story 2 does not say this, it is a narrowing of FR-010 and needs a ruling.

decisions.summary: Restatement of D1-D6; code map; perf bookends at T04 and T12, speed a flag not a gate.
decisions.why: These record facts and practice. They make no decision the spec leaves open.

decisions.summary: Fresh block of 500 after each engine landing, 1,000 at T01 and close; SC-001's N is 500; the landing's own fresh block (FR-009) stays the cohort gate's 48.
decisions.why: SC-001 sets N at least 500 and leaves the number to the plan; 500 is its floor. FR-009 names 'the fresh block', which is feature 415 D5's FRESH=48 (quoted in spec-cited), so 48 is the spec's size, not a plan narrowing of 'all seeds pass'. The 500/1,000 blocks are extra measurement inside 417 serving FR-001 and SC-001.

decisions.summary: make fresh-tally reads dev/cohort-log records and prints the pooled fresh rate by form and cause.
decisions.why: Tooling for FR-001's measurement, reproducing the spec's gap method; adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: Inventory found by search (STEPS, after-the-web passes, cohort_audit rules and their callers, mid-map callers of the law/row/grove/overlap checks, pairs judging one rule, every refusal/drop site where room is the remedy); each entry records which of the four points it breaks or that its rule is coded twice, with its R1 share; a non-breaking entry is kept with its predicate; every breaking entry becomes a task.
decisions.why: Covers all four of FR-002's categories and FR-007's room sites; the four points are the rule the GM agreed (point 3 'run in the generator' matches 'keep one finished-map check per rule, in the cohort and the tests only'); every breaking entry being a task closes round 1's finding that classification could leave entries unworked. FR-002 also asks each entry's location ('where it is'); D3's search yields it but does not list it among the recorded fields - T03 must record it. A missing field, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: make task-start refuses a task of a feature marked ON HOLD until an open feature closes; HOLD_OK admits only a non-engine task (judged by the task's research: line); an engine task of a held feature has no escape.
decisions.why: FR-010 forbids starting an engine-changing task of a claims feature until 417 closes; D4 now gives that no escape, closing round 1's finding. Holding non-engine tasks by default is stricter than FR-010 and matches the GM's 'put our claims work on hold'. Two premises are not verifiable from the bundle and the implementation must make them hold: the research: line must reliably mark every engine task (a mislabelled engine task would pass HOLD_OK), and the guard reaches only features marked ON HOLD, so 'any other claims feature the session finds' is enforced once found and marked.

decisions.summary: Engine tasks ordered by share of R1's failures: lane web, seating room, row/brook/grove rules into placers, then the rest; each task's design decided in its Approach first.
decisions.why: The spec leaves order open; the lane web first is what the session proposed and the GM accepted. Ordering narrows nothing - every inventory entry is still worked.

decisions.summary: FR-003's principle text drafted at T03 and the constitution amended only with the GM's words.
decisions.why: FR-003 verbatim: 'in text the GM approves'.

decisions.summary: The landing guards (FR-009 fresh block before the push, FR-011 forms against HEAD) go on once a fresh block of 500 passes whole.
decisions.why: FR-009 'once SC-001 is met'; FR-011 meets 394's deferral by building after SC-001.

decisions.summary: make perf at start and end; speed is a flag, never a gate.
decisions.why: Restates the standing rule (375 amendment 5); narrows nothing in this request.

decisions.summary: Each engine task runs the reference map, make land, and a background fresh block of 500 after its landing.
decisions.why: Before SC-001 the spec does not gate fresh seeds at landing (FR-009 starts after SC-001); FR-008's fixed/pinned/pool regression gate stays.

decisions.summary: Lane-law rules and research claims are not altered, only asked earlier; a rule that cannot be asked before placing is a research question and goes to the record first.
decisions.why: Within only because D3 makes every breaking entry a task regardless; the clause routes a hard case to research, it does not keep a repair pass. A later plan-delta that uses this clause to keep a place-then-repair pass or a generator-run finished-map check is a narrowing of the GM's 'not something we want anywhere' and is owed its own MODE 1 ruling.

decisions.summary: During rebuilds that re-deal maps, the fresh rate must not rise and each newly failing fresh seed is diagnosed in the task's notes; fixed or pinned regressions block a landing.
decisions.why: Stricter than the spec, which does not gate fresh seeds before SC-001; it addresses the GM's 'making some seeds pass just ends up breaking other seeds' rather than excusing it, and FR-008 is untouched.

decisions.summary: A defect found in code a task does not change becomes a task in 417.
decisions.why: Keeps found work in scope; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: T01 measure, T02 hold guard, T03 inventory and principle draft, T04 onward one engine task per inventory group, T10 FR-009, T11 FR-011/SC-006, T12 close (1,000 fresh, T106 seat turn, SC-004 delta, report).
decisions.why: One task per group is granularity, provided every breaking entry of D3 lands in some task, which D3 requires. The fixed T10-T12 numbering leaves six engine slots; plan-delta adds tasks as found, so it is drafting, not a cap on scope.

decisions.summary: Technical Context: the lane web's size now a labeled one-shot count; the reference map's time stated as the cohort's own 60 s budget; the single-artifact target (Inashiro, then cohort and a fresh block) unchanged
decisions.why: Descriptive context and figure labeling only; the two-step engine task (reference map, then cohort and fresh block) serves FR-001/SC-001 as judged CLEAR before.

decisions.summary: perf bookends at T04 and at the close, the close now 'the last task' instead of T12; speed a flag, never a gate
decisions.why: Renumbering only; nothing the request or spec asks is narrowed, and speed was never a requirement of the request.

decisions.summary: fresh block of 500 after each engine landing, 1,000 at T01 and the close, SC-001's N = 500, the landing's own block stays 48; timings now labeled (2.8 s a seed, one-shot 2026-10-24)
decisions.why: Sets N at the spec's floor of 500 (SC-001 'at least 500'); the timing change is a label only. The 48-seed in-landing block is the FR-009 gate; SC-001's N governs the 'all seeds pass' measure, as judged CLEAR in round 2.

decisions.summary: a fresh-seed tally script reading the cohort logs by form and cause
decisions.why: Unchanged; serves FR-001's measurement.

decisions.summary: the inventory's method, each entry now recording its location (file and function) as well as the point it breaks and its share of failures; every breaking entry becomes a task
decisions.why: Adding the location widens what each entry carries; it narrows nothing. The inventory answers the GM's 'Where else is this part of our algorithm?' and FR-002.

decisions.summary: the hold enforced by make task-start on features whose status line says ON HOLD until 417 closes; reaches each claims feature once its status says so, each one found later marked when found; HOLD_OK admits only non-engine tasks; no escape for an engine task
decisions.why: FR-010 holds engine-changing tasks of 405, 372, 384 and any claims feature the session finds; the plan obliges marking each found feature when found, so the status-line mechanism reaches every feature FR-010 names (372 and 384 already marked beside 405). Admitting non-engine tasks is FR-010's own scope ('that changes the engine'), not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: engine tasks ordered by share of R1's failures (lane web, seating room, row/brook/grove rules, the rest), each designed in its Approach first
decisions.why: Unchanged but for figure labels; the lane web first is what the GM approved ('the lane web first' was proposed and accepted with 'Yes please').

decisions.summary: FR-003's principle drafted by T03 and amended into the constitution only with the GM's words
decisions.why: Unchanged; FR-003 requires text the GM approves.

decisions.summary: T01 measure, T02 hold guard, T03 inventory and principle draft, T04 onward engine tasks numbered as the inventory needs, then the two guard tasks (FR-009 fresh block before the push; FR-011/SC-006 every form against HEAD), then the closing task (1,000 seeds, T106's seat turn re-applied, SC-004 delta, report)
decisions.why: Removing the fixed T10-T12 numbers lets the engine work run as many tasks as the inventory finds; every task the earlier Order carried is still present in the same sequence. FR-009 and FR-011 still follow SC-001's engine work, as FR-009 ('once SC-001 is met') and FR-011 ('building it after SC-001') require.

blocks: ## T01 - the baseline and the tally (FR-001)

decisions.summary: T01 baseline is seeds 3000101-3001100 (1,000) rolled FRESH=0 at main in a detached worktree, five workers
decisions.why: D1 sets 1,000 at T01; the size and the at-main, no-diff constraint are kept. Five workers instead of D1's twelve moves only the wall clock, not N or what is measured.

decisions.summary: make fresh-tally takes COMMIT= and SINCE=, defines which records count as fresh, one seed counted once per commit
decisions.why: The instrument for FR-001's rate 'by form and by cause, at the start and after each task that changes the engine'. It counts seeds the gate has never used and narrows nothing the spec asked to measure.

decisions.summary: T01 done = research R3 holds the 1,000-seed table by form and cause, with a test that is red without it
decisions.why: FR-001's start measurement. The test only enforces that the requested table exists (enforcement of the request, not scope).

decisions.summary: T02 lands second, alone, via make land-tooling; HOLD_OK only for a non-engine task
decisions.why: Same as D4: HOLD_OK admits only a non-engine task, and an engine task of a held feature has no escape.

decisions.summary: Held feature = Status line holds ON HOLD and 'until feature NNN', NNN open by speckit-todo's rule; engine task = names a path under l7r/ or pool/, or research: physical, or names a decision whose plan section names such a path; unsure counts as engine
decisions.why: A superset of D4's test (D4 checks the research: line, D9 adds paths and decision references and defaults to engine when unsure). Refusing more can only strengthen FR-010's hold; it makes no claims-feature engine task startable that D4 would refuse. It sits within the GM's 'put our claims work on hold'. Note: the hold reaches a feature only once its Status line is marked (D4). FR-010 names 405, 372 and 384, and these blocks do not say 372 and 384 get marked. T02's test uses 405 only. The session must mark all three. The blocks do not decide against it, so this is not ruled a narrowing.

decisions.summary: T03 after T01 (its causes rank the entries); one task per breaking group; the principle's draft text in R4 for the GM
decisions.why: D3: 'Every entry that breaks a point becomes a task'. Grouping still puts each breaking entry in a task. FR-003: 'in text the GM approves', and the draft goes to the GM. Ranking by R1/T01 causes matches D3's 'its share of R1's failures'.

decisions.summary: The inventory reading is split by package (ways, homesteads/homestead_parts, waterfields, overlap registry, the rest), each package read by a sonnet Explore agent given 'D3's four questions'; the session checks each REPORTED entry against the code
decisions.why: FR-002 asks that EVERY repair pass, finished-map-only rule, rule coded more than once and in-generator check be listed. D3 makes that a method of enumerated searches: (1) every STEPS function and after-the-web pass; (2) every cohort_audit rule with its callers inside l7r/; (3) every caller of law.violations, lane_violators, row_rules, grove_rules and the overlap matrix inside the generator's run; (4) every pair of functions judging one rule; (5) every no-candidate drop/relax/refuse site. Entries are classed against the four points OR as 'its rule is coded twice'. D10 narrows this in two ways. (a) 'D3's four questions' does not match D3. There are four points plus a fifth class, coded-twice, and five searches. Whichever four are meant, one of D3's searches is not asked: coded-twice if the four are the points, the refusal sites if they are FR-002's four kinds. (b) Searches (2), (3) and (4) cross package lines. They follow a rule into cohort_audit, a check function to its callers inside the generator, and one rule to its second implementation. The likeliest duplicate, a rule in a placer package and again in the audit or check, lands in two different agents' reads, and neither sees the pair. The session checking each reported entry keeps a fetched claim out of R2 but finds nothing no agent reported, so completeness ('every', SC-007) is lost. A per-package split is not impossible to square with D3, so the narrowing is not forced. Fix: give each agent D3's full search list, coded-twice named. The session runs searches (2), (3) and (4) over the whole tree itself and reconciles their hits against R2 before T03 is done.

blocks: ## T01 - the baseline and the tally (FR-001)

decisions.summary: Baseline is 1,000 fresh seeds 3000101-3001100 at main in a detached worktree, FRESH=0, five workers for memory.
decisions.why: Carries FR-001's start-of-feature measurement at D1's T01 size of 1,000 on main's engine with no diff; the worker count is execution, not scope.

decisions.summary: make fresh-tally filters by COMMIT=/SINCE=, defines which records' seeds count as fresh, one seed counted once per commit.
decisions.why: The instrument FR-001 needs to read a fresh-seed rate by form and cause; the freshness rule keeps fixed-range and pinned seeds out, which is what 'fresh' means in the request.

decisions.summary: T01 first; done when R3 holds the 1,000-seed table by form and cause and the tally's test is red without it.
decisions.why: Matches FR-001 and D1; the test enforces the requested measurement.

decisions.summary: Held = Status line with ON HOLD and 'until feature NNN', NNN open by speckit-todo's rule; engine task = names a path under l7r/ or pool/, or research: physical, or names a decision whose plan section names such a path; unsure counts as engine.
decisions.why: Implements D4's status-line trigger; the engine-task test is broader than D4's research:-line check and resolves doubt toward holding, so it widens FR-010's reach rather than narrowing it.

decisions.summary: Guard in make task-start, landed alone by land-tooling; HOLD_OK only for a non-engine task; done when 405, 372 and 384 carry ON HOLD and the refusal/HOLD_OK tests are red without the guard.
decisions.why: FR-010 names 405, 372 and 384 and D4 requires the hold to reach a feature through its status line; the done line now marks all three, and the tests only enforce the requested hold.

decisions.summary: Per-package Explore agents on sonnet run D3's five searches and five classes, every reported entry checked against the code by the session; the session itself runs the three cross-package searches (cohort_audit rules and callers, callers of the mid-map checks, pairs judging one rule) over the whole tree and reconciles their hits against R2 before T03 is done.
decisions.why: Round 1's defect is cured: the agents now carry the coded-twice class and all five searches, and the searches a package split cannot see whole are run over the whole tree by the session and reconciled. The remaining two searches (stage.py STEPS / after-the-web passes, and no-candidate drop sites) are local to a placer or a file and the package partition (with 'the rest') covers the tree. Delegating the reading under that method does not reduce what FR-002/D3 require to be listed.

decisions.summary: Inventory after T01 (its causes rank entries); non-breaking entries kept with their predicate; done when R2 is complete, one task per breaking group is in tasks.md, and the principle's draft text is in R4 for the GM.
decisions.why: Follows FR-002, D3 (kept-with-predicate, every breaking entry becomes a task - grouped entries are still each carried by a task) and FR-003 (text for the GM to approve).

blocks: ## T01 - the baseline and the tally (FR-001)

decisions.summary: The T01 baseline is the 1,000 seeds 3000101-3001100, rolled at main in a detached worktree (make cohort N=1000 SEED=3000101 FRESH=0 JOBS=5), with no rendering.
decisions.why: FR-001 asks for the fresh-seed failure rate measured at the start, on a block whose size the plan sets, and D1 sets 1,000 at T01. Rolling at main with no diff is that start. A seed range above the fixed cohort is the 'seeds nobody has used' the request's 14% figure was about. Five workers instead of D1's estimate at 12 changes only the wall time; D1's 12 is an input to its time estimate, not a requirement. Nothing in the request or spec is cut.

decisions.summary: make fresh-tally filters records by COMMIT= and SINCE=, counts a seed as fresh when it is at or above its record's fresh_first or, for a FRESH=0 roll, when the record's first seed is above the fixed range and the pinned rows, counts each seed once per commit, and has no rendering.
decisions.why: This is the tool that produces FR-001's measurement: a rate by form and cause at one engine commit, which FR-001 requires 'at the start and after each task that changes the engine'. The fresh rule leaves out the fixed cohort and the pinned rows, which are not fresh seeds in the request's sense, so it narrows nothing. Counting once per commit stops a re-rolled seed from inflating or deflating the rate. Its test serves FR-001 and adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: A held feature is one whose **Status** line holds `ON HOLD` and `until feature NNN`, with NNN open by speckit-todo's own open/closed rule.
decisions.why: D4 names exactly this status form (`ON HOLD ... until feature NNN ... closes` while NNN is open); reusing the existing open/closed rule implements FR-010's 'until this feature closes' without changing what is held.

decisions.summary: An engine task is one that names a path under l7r/ or pool/, or whose research: line is physical, or that names a decision whose plan section names such a path; unsure counts as engine.
decisions.why: FR-010 holds every task that changes the engine; D4 has the guard read the research: line. The extra triggers and 'unsure counts as engine' only widen what is refused, so the hold covers more engine tasks, never fewer. Nothing the request asked to hold is let through.

decisions.summary: HOLD_OK admits a non-engine task only; an engine task has no escape.
decisions.why: Restates D4: HOLD_OK only for a task that does not change the engine, and an engine task of a held feature has no escape.

decisions.summary: 405, 372 and 384 carry the ON HOLD status (marked 2026-10-24), and tests show an engine task of 405 refused (naming 417), HOLD_OK on it refused, a non-engine task with HOLD_OK started, each red without the guard.
decisions.why: FR-010 names 405, 372 and 384, and D4 has later-found claims features marked when found. The tests only fail when the requested hold is missing, so they enforce the request.

decisions.summary: Second task, small, lands alone via make land-tooling.
decisions.why: Sequencing only. It puts the hold in place early and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: T03 runs after T01, whose measured causes rank the inventory's entries.
decisions.why: D3 asks each entry to carry its share of R1's failures; sequencing the inventory after the measurement that supplies those shares serves that and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: An entry that breaks no point is kept, listed with the predicate that makes it so.
decisions.why: Restates D3 ('an entry that breaks none is listed as kept with the predicate that makes it so'); it does not let any breaking entry escape a task.

decisions.summary: 3 h budget.
decisions.why: A planning estimate; it removes no search or class from the inventory, and the done-criterion (R2 complete) is what closes the task, not the clock.

decisions.summary: Done when R2 is complete, one task per breaking group is filed in tasks.md (Approach added by plan-delta at start), and the principle's draft text is in R4 for the GM.
decisions.why: D3: every entry that breaks a point becomes a task - grouping breaking entries into tasks still gives every such entry a task, provided each entry belongs to a group (it must, for R2 to be 'complete'). FR-003: the rule enters the constitution 'in text the GM approves' - a draft placed for the GM is that, not a self-approval. The GM's 'anywhere in the codebase' is preserved: nothing here limits where entries are sought.

decisions.summary: Reading split by package (ways; homesteads and homestead_parts; waterfields; overlap registry; the rest), each by an Explore agent on sonnet given D3's whole method (five searches, the four points plus coded-twice); every reported entry checked by the session against the code before entering R2; the three cross-package searches (cohort_audit rules with callers in l7r/, callers of law.violations / lane_violators / row_rules / grove_rules / overlap matrix inside the run, pairs of functions judging one rule) run by the session over the whole tree and reconciled against R2. Rendering none.
decisions.why: A division of labour, not of scope: the partition ends in 'the rest', so the whole tree is read, matching the GM's 'anywhere in the codebase' and FR-002's 'every'. Each agent gets all of D3's searches and classes, the cross-package searches D3 names are run whole-tree rather than per package (so a package boundary cannot hide a caller or a twin), and the session's code check of every reported entry keeps D3's 'found, not remembered' (an agent's claim is not an entry). 'Rendering: none' matches D3.

blocks: ## T04 - one stream-crossing rule (R2 G7; FR-006)

decisions.summary: Block sizes, tally, inventory method, the hold, order, the principle - byte-identical to the text judged CLEAR (diffed against earlier.md).
decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict; nothing new to rule on.

decisions.summary: The stop line: the FR-004/FR-005/FR-006 conversions are done; no work aimed at the fresh rate and no FR-007 room work until the GM resumes it.
decisions.why: Narrows the accepted spec (SC-001, FR-007 stay open), but it is the GM's own 2026-10-25 words: finish the tasks that turn off automated checks and replace them with placing correctly first, then stop before 'the actual fixing where we get more seeds to pass'. Room work (FR-007) and fresh-rate work exist to get more seeds passing, so they fall on the side of the line the GM set down. Implied by the GM's words, not completed for them.

decisions.summary: A conversion that cannot land green (FR-008) without seed-by-seed work or room is recorded and set down, never iterated on; each conversion lands through make land when FR-008 holds, its fresh rate recorded either way.
decisions.why: Iterating a conversion until cohort seeds pass is the seed-fixing the GM asked to go through 'slowly and deliberately' with them; setting it down at that point is what the GM's words require. Landing only with FR-008 holding keeps the spec's no-regression rule; FR-009's refusal applies only once SC-001 is met, so not invoking it now is the spec read literally.

decisions.summary: A rule coded twice with different values is made one at the lane law's (or the rule's own recorded) value; one with no recorded value waits for the GM.
decisions.why: Taking the lane law's or recorded value is FR-004/FR-006 read literally (each lane-law rule stays one predicate in law.py; the check calls the placer's predicate). The deferral of a rule with no recorded value narrows FR-006 for that rule, but choosing an unrecorded value is a constant decision that moves maps - part of the deliberate fixing the GM reserved for themselves - so it is implied by the stop line. Adjudicated separately from D11a/b.

decisions.summary: No T20/T21 until the GM resumes it.
decisions.why: CONDITIONAL: the bundle does not identify T20/T21. LEGITIMATE only if they are fresh-rate, room, close or SC-001-dependent tasks (e.g. the FR-009 refusal, which the spec itself conditions on SC-001 being met). If either is a no-map task (FR-003's principle text, FR-011's gate, inventory or tooling), deferring it is outside the GM's stop line, which deferred only the fixing - and this ruling does not cover it. The caller must confirm what T20/T21 are.

decisions.summary: The tasks that move no map go first (reorders D5's share-of-failures order).
decisions.why: Task order is the plan's to choose; the lane-web-first order was the session's proposal, not the GM's words, and running no-map tasks first serves the stop line.

decisions.summary: T04 Approach: the cohort audit's 'farmstead part across the brook' adopts the placers' crosses_a_stream; the audit's own _cross is deleted; the audit keeps its part list and count; T04 runs first as it moves no map.
decisions.why: FR-006 verbatim: a finished-map check calls its placer's predicate and a second implementation is deleted. The direction (placer's predicate wins) is the spec's. The boundary difference item 4 names (strict vs one-side non-strict) is the disagreement FR-006 exists to remove. Item 9's test only enforces FR-006 and is not added scope.

decisions.why: FR-001 asks for the fresh-seed failure rate measured at the start, on a block whose size the plan sets, and D1 sets 1,000 at T01. Rolling at main with no diff is that start. A seed range above the fixed cohort is the 'seeds nobody has used' the request's 14% figure was about. Five workers instead of D1's estimate at 12 changes only the wall time; D1's 12 is an input to its time estimate, not a requirement. Nothing in the request or spec is cut.

decisions.summary: make fresh-tally filters records by COMMIT= and SINCE=, counts a seed as fresh when it is at or above its record's fresh_first or, for a FRESH=0 roll, when the record's first seed is above the fixed range and the pinned rows, counts each seed once per commit, and has no rendering.
decisions.why: This is the tool that produces FR-001's measurement: a rate by form and cause at one engine commit, which FR-001 requires 'at the start and after each task that changes the engine'. The fresh rule leaves out the fixed cohort and the pinned rows, which are not fresh seeds in the request's sense, so it narrows nothing. Counting once per commit stops a re-rolled seed from inflating or deflating the rate. Its test serves FR-001 and adds no behavior.
